comparator.route: Spanish Language and Culture specialisation with two supplementary Spanish minors and the standard third-year Spanish-speaking study abroad
comparator.sourceNotes: This normalized target is the Spanish Language and Culture specialisation within Romance Languages and Cultures, not a generic humanities bachelor. Official prospective year pages give 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of 60 EC compulsory Spanish language acquisition (four 5-EC courses), Spanish/Hispanic culture, media, literature, linguistics and humanities study; two 0-EC mentoring/language-skill units are omitted. Year two has 30 EC compulsory Spanish language, linguistics, culture and literature, plus two required 15-EC arts minors. The route selects supplementary Spanish minor 1 and 2 in published order, each consisting of three 5-EC courses; the alternative 5-EC Academicus voor de klas course is unselected. Year three consists of a compulsory 15-EC Spanish-speaking study abroad component, a 5-EC Hispanic major course, 30 EC genuinely open free space and a 10-EC bachelor thesis. The abroad major component and free space remain separate even where some free courses are taken abroad. The prospective year pages form a coherent indicative cohort sequence; final course availability and requirements should be checked against the applicable catalogue.

routeSelection.basis: The target names the Spanish specialisation specifically. For its two 15-EC arts minor choices, the two numbered supplementary Spanish minors and their first three listed courses instantiate a coherent language-area route independently of UCR fit; the 30-EC third-year free space remains open.

exception.reason: The programme is built around progressive Spanish-language proficiency (Español 1–6), Spanish-language study of literature, linguistic variation, media, culture and politics of Spain and Latin America, a credited 15-EC study period at a Spanish-speaking university, and an independent Hispanic studies thesis. Even after preserving 30 EC of third-year free space, there is no 24-course UCR curriculum with sustained Spanish language instruction and advanced Hispanic literature/culture/linguistics in the medium of Spanish. A general culture, communication or history programme would erase the defining language and regional specialisation.
exception.curriculumContext: One named Spanish specialisation has 60 compulsory EC in year one, 30 core plus 30 restricted arts-minor EC in year two, and 15 abroad-major + 5 Hispanic-major + 30 genuinely free + 10 thesis EC in year three. The arts-minor units are selected choices, not all possible electives simultaneously; the optional education-related course is excluded from the selected first minor. Abroad and free-space credits are kept separate despite their possible shared location.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook course rows and their descriptions, topic/profile enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. MCCCOMM112 offers introductory Dutch rather than Spanish. MCCCOMM211/311 study language style, meaning and persuasion; HCBCOGN312 addresses psycholinguistics; MCCLITR112/211/312 study world literature and interpretation; MCCHEAM111/112/211 and GOSHIST111/211 support broad cultural, historical and material-heritage questions. None supplies sequenced Spanish language learning, Hispanic literature and region-specific advanced study, Spanish-medium academic work or a required Spanish-speaking study-abroad major and Hispanic thesis. The adjacent courses cannot be presented as a defensible equivalent 24-course response to this named language specialisation.
